questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.
The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.
At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.
Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harappan burial practices** reflect the socio-cultural and religious beliefs of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The dead were generally laid in **rectangular or oval-shaped pits**, which were dug specifically for burial purposes.
 
• Burials could be classified into three main types: **primary burials** (where the body is buried intact), **secondary burials** (where only the bones are buried after the decomposition), and **fractional burials** (partial burial).
 
• Some burials were accompanied by **grave goods**, including pottery, tools, ornaments, and occasionally food items, suggesting a belief in life after death.
 
• Harappan burial sites such as **Kalibangan, Lothal, and Rakhigarhi** provide archaeological evidence of these practices.
 
• The orientation of the buried bodies varied, with some placed in a **north-south direction** and others in an **east-west direction.**
 
• Occasionally, communal graves were found, indicating the practice of **group burials.**
 
• These burial customs highlight the advanced cultural practices and spiritual beliefs of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.**__

 __
 
• The statement is incorrect because the **Harappan civilization** extended beyond Sindh and Punjab, spanning regions of **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and even parts of Maharashtra.**
 
• Important sites include **Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa (Pakistan), Lothal and Dholavira (Gujarat), Kalibangan (Rajasthan), and Rakhigarhi (Haryana).**
 
• This wide geographical spread reflects the vastness of the **Indus Valley Civilization.**
 
 
 
• **The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.**__
 __
 
• The statement is incorrect because the **Harappan script** remains undeciphered to date.
 
• The script consists of **pictographs and symbols**, with over 400 unique signs identified.
 
• It is believed to be written from **right to left** in some cases and **left to right** in others.
 
• The inability to decipher the script limits our understanding of the **language, administration, and beliefs** of the Harappan people.
 
 
 
• **Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.**__
 
 
• This statement is incorrect as granaries were found in multiple Harappan sites such as **Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, and Rakhigarhi.**
 
• Granaries were massive structures used for storing **grain**, showcasing the importance of agriculture in the Harappan economy.
 
• The granaries in Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro are particularly notable for their **engineering and layout.**

questions.question: Harappa, one of the sites of the Harappan culture, was found in which of the following states of pre-independent India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harappa** was one of the most significant cities of the **Indus Valley Civilization** and is an archaeological site situated in present-day **Pakistan's Punjab province**.
 
• During **pre-independent India**, this region was part of the larger Punjab province under British rule.
 
• Harappa was discovered in the early **1920s** by **Daya Ram Sahni** under the supervision of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).**
 
• The site is known for its advanced urban planning, including features like a sophisticated **drainage system**, well-structured houses, and a unique grid-based street layout.
 
• Artifacts such as **seals, pottery, beads, and tools** have been uncovered, offering insights into the culture, trade, and daily life of the Harappan people.
 
• The city is believed to have been a major center of trade and administration during the peak of the **Indus Valley Civilization (2600–1900 BCE).**
 
• The name "Harappan Civilization" is derived from this site, as it was the first city of the civilization to be excavated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Balochistan**__

 __
 
• **Balochistan** is a province in present-day Pakistan, but it was not the location of Harappa. However, another significant Indus Valley site, **Mehrgarh**, is located in Balochistan.
 
• **Mehrgarh** is one of the earliest known agricultural settlements (7000 BCE) and predates the Harappan Civilization.
 
 
 
• **Sindh**__
 __
 
• **Sindh** is a province in present-day Pakistan and was part of pre-independent India's Bombay Presidency.
 
• It is home to another major Indus Valley site, **Mohenjo-daro**, known for its advanced urban features and iconic "Great Bath."
 
 
 
• **United Province**__
 
 
• The **United Province** (modern-day Uttar Pradesh) in pre-independent India was not associated with the Harappan sites.
 
• This region was historically significant for other cultures and civilizations, such as the **Vedic Period** and the **Mauryan Empire**, but not the Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Iron Age in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrauli iron pillar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mehrauli iron pillar is a historical monument located in Delhi, India.
 
• This pillar is famous for its rust-resistant composition of metals and dates back to the Gupta period (around the 4th century AD).
 
• It is not associated with the Iron Age in India, which primarily spans from around 1500 BC to 200 BC.
 
• The pillar is believed to have been constructed during the reign of Chandragupta II (375-415 AD).
 
• The pillar's inscription and construction techniques are distinct from those of the Iron Age, which makes it an exceptional artifact from the Gupta period rather than the Iron Age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Age in India**

 
 
• The Iron Age in India began around 1500 BC and lasted until approximately 200 BC.
 
• This period is characterized by the widespread use of iron tools and weapons, which significantly enhanced agricultural productivity and warfare.
 
• Notable cultures from this period include the Painted Grey Ware culture and the Northern Black Polished Ware culture.
 
• Iron smelting and metallurgy were significant advancements during this time, leading to the development of more durable and efficient tools.
 
 
 
• **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)**
 
 
• PGW is a type of pottery associated with the Vedic period in northern India.
 
• It dates back to the Iron Age and is characterized by its grey color and painted geometric designs.
 
• PGW sites are often linked to the early Indo-Aryan settlements in the region.
 
 
 
• **Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW)**
 
 
• NBPW is a type of fine pottery that emerged during the later part of the Iron Age in India, around 700-200 BC.
 
• This pottery is known for its highly polished black surface and was used by the Mauryan Empire and other contemporary cultures.
 
• NBPW is considered a hallmark of urbanization and socio-economic development in ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Period**
 
 
• The Gupta period, spanning from the 4th to the 6th century AD, is known as the Golden Age of India.
 
• This era witnessed significant advancements in science, mathematics, astronomy, religion, and art.
 
• The Mehrauli iron pillar is an example of the high level of metallurgical skill achieved during this time.

questions.question: In Dholavira, which of the following materials is extensively used as a building material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dholavira, one of the most prominent archaeological sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, extensively utilized **stone** as a primary building material.
 
• The city’s structures, including walls, reservoirs, and gateways, were constructed using locally available stone, especially **sandstone and limestone**.
 
• Unlike other Harappan sites that predominantly used bricks, Dholavira is unique for its reliance on stone due to its geographical location in the arid region of Gujarat.
 
• The use of stone ensured durability and adaptability to the harsh climate of the Rann of Kutch, where Dholavira is located.
 
• The site’s sophisticated water management system, including reservoirs and drains, was also carved from stone, showcasing advanced engineering techniques of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dholavira:**

 
 
• Dholavira is located in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, and is one of the largest Harappan settlements in India.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its unique urban planning and water conservation systems.
 
 
 
• **Water Management System:**
 
 
• Dholavira is famous for its intricate water management system, including reservoirs, step wells, and drains.
 
• This system reflects the ingenuity of the Harappan civilization in adapting to a water-scarce environment.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Architecture:**
 
 
• The Harappan civilization is known for its urban planning, including grid-patterned streets, drainage systems, and standardized building materials like bricks and stones.
 
 
 
• **Materials Used in Harappan Sites:**
 
 
• While baked and unbaked bricks were common in most Harappan sites, Dholavira stands out for its extensive use of stone due to the availability of local resources.
 
• Other materials used included wood and mud for specific purposes like roofing and insulation.

questions.question: Which was the first ancient Indian civilization that had systematic town planning and underground drainage systems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Indus Valley civilization.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indus Valley civilization is one of the earliest civilizations in the world and flourished around 2600 BCE.**
 
• The Indus Valley civilization was notable for its advanced town planning**, which included well-organized streets, drainage systems, and public buildings.**
 
• The ancient cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro in the Indus Valley region had well-planned streets, public baths, and underground drainage systems ahead of their time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Nubian civilization** refers to the civilization that emerged in the **Nile Valley around 2000 BCE.** Still, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems in this civilization.
 
• **Later Vedic civilization **refers to the period of Indian history tha**t followed the decline of the Indus Valley civilization,** and while this period saw the emergence of the caste system and the Vedas, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems.
 
• **Aegean civilization** refers to the civilizations that emerged in the Aegean region, including the Minoan and Mycenaean civilizations, but while these civilizations had impressive art and architecture, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems.

questions.question: Which among the following is a Harappan city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dholavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dholavira** is an archaeological site in **Khadirbet, Bhachau Taluka, Kutch District, Gujarat**, named after a modern-day town 1 kilometre south of it. Radhanpur is 165 kilometres away from this settlement.
 
• The site, also known locally as Kotada timba, features the ruins of an old** Indus Valley Civilization settlement**.
 
• **The Tropic of Cancer** runs through Dholavira. It is one of the five major Harappan sites in India and one of the most important Indus Valley Civilization archaeological sites.
 
• It is also thought to have been the most magnificent city of its period.
 
• It's on Khadir Bet Island in the Great Rann of Kutch's Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indus Valley Civilisation**, also known as the Harappan Civilisation or the Indus Civilisation, was a Bronze Age civilisation in northwestern South Asia that lasted from 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE, and from 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE in its mature form.
 
• It thrived in the Indus River basins, which flows through the length of Pakistan, and along a system of perennial, largely monsoon-fed rivers that originally ran across northwest India and eastern Pakistan near the seasonal Ghaggar-Hakra river.
 
• **Lumbini** is a Buddhist pilgrimage place in Nepal's Lumbini Province's Rupandehi District. 
 
• **The Empire of Kosala **was an ancient Indian kingdom with a rich culture that spanned the territory from modern-day Uttar Pradesh to Western Odisha.
 
• **Hampi** is a historic village in Karnataka, India's southernmost state. Numerous damaged temple complexes from the Vijayanagara Empire dot the landscape.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE for the Harappan town planning?

1. Most of the towns have citadel in harappan civilization.

2. Every town had a temple in Harappan civilization.

3. Every building was made of sand stone in Harappan civilization.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Harappan civilization is known for its advanced town planning, including features like grid layouts and well-organized drainage systems.
 
• Most Harappan towns had a citadel, which served as a fortified area housing important buildings and possibly administrative centers.
 
• There is no evidence that every town had a temple; instead, the civilization is known for its secular architecture.
 
• Harappan buildings were primarily constructed using baked bricks, not sandstone.
 
• The cities featured well-planned streets, granaries, and public baths, reflecting advanced urban planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citadel:** A raised area in Harappan cities that housed important buildings and possibly served as a center for administration and storage.
 
• **Drainage System:** Harappan cities had sophisticated drainage systems with covered drains running alongside the streets, indicating advanced engineering skills.
 
• **Granaries:** Large storage structures found in some Harappan cities, suggesting the importance of agriculture and surplus storage in their economy.
 
• **Public Baths:** Structures like the Great Bath in Mohenjo-Daro, indicating the emphasis on cleanliness and possibly ritual bathing in Harappan culture.
 
• **Urban Planning:** The layout of Harappan cities with grid-pattern streets, standardized brick sizes, and consistent architectural planning across various settlements.
